faq.q: What is an AI image to video tool?
faq.a: It turns a product photo into a moving video with a casual phone-video look (called UGC). You can add a script, an AI person, a spoken voice, captions and a song from the music library. Then post it, or download it with no watermark.

faq.q: How does a photo become a video?
faq.a: Upload the image or paste a product link. Motion comes from what you describe. You can set captions, a script and a spoken voice before you download.

faq.q: What do you gain by making video from a photo?
faq.a: You can make several versions from a photo you already sell. Credits are the points a video spends. A 6-second clip is 24 credits. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits. You are not booking a filming day. The same photo can run as tall 9:16, square 1:1, wide 16:9, 4:3 or 3:4.

faq.q: Can I post these clips on social?
faq.a: Yes. Make them for TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and ordinary posts. Then post to TikTok or Meta in one click, or download the file. Check each app's current rules.

faq.q: How can a store use this for product marketing?
faq.a: Make a product showcase, a before-and-after, a social ad or a listing video for Amazon and other marketplaces that allow video. Make several versions at once, then keep the first line that works.

faq.q: Can I make explainers and tutorials?
faq.a: Yes. Use the same AI person and script to explain a feature or a short how-to. Each lesson then looks the same.

faq.q: Can I add a spoken voice or a person on screen?
faq.a: Yes. A script writer, a spoken voice, captions and the actor library are included. The actor library is a set of ready-made AI people. You can speak the script in another language. You can swap a song from the music library. You can trim the clip in the built-in editor. An API is a connection that lets your own tools start the same job.

faq.q: Which shapes and lengths can I pick?
faq.a: Pick a video shape: tall 9:16, square 1:1, wide 16:9, 4:3 or 3:4. 4:3 is a little wide, and 3:4 is a little tall. Lengths are 6, 10, 15 or 30 seconds. Those cost 24, 40, 60 or 120 credits, in that order. Credits are the points a video spends. If a video fails, those credits come back.
